audit_findings.title: Finite, noncash 45Z benefit may have been capitalized as perpetual owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.1 million fiscal-2025 benefit, equal to 50.1% of the $56.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The benefit enters anchor OE and is then grown and capitalized in terminal value despite statutory expiration after 2029.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2025, the Company recognized an income tax benefit for federal 45Z clean fuel production credits of approximately $ 28.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated finite benefit and an unresolved anchor error. The filings confirm the benefit was recognized, while the valuation does not show its removal or a finite credit schedule. Because it equals about half the anchor, perpetual capitalization is reasonably capable of changing every scenario materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct anchor OE excluding 45Z, then rerun with separately modeled cash proceeds, compliance costs and utilization through 2029; thereafter apply normalized taxes and include 45Q only if its required investment and operating assumptions are modeled.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to give common shareholders 100% of subsidiary cash despite minority claims
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash and short-term investments to common equity without deducting the portions economically attributable to noncontrolling owners or required inside subsidiaries.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash and short-term investments balance of approximately $375.8 million at January 31, 2026 included approximately $336.5 million held by One Earth and NuGen.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim mismatch is demonstrated: REX owns 76.1% of One Earth and 99.7% of NuGen, while $336.5 million of the January 2026 $375.8 million cash and short-term-investment balance was held by those subsidiaries. The latest legal-entity split is unavailable, so the exact overstatement cannot be established, but the concentration at partially owned subsidiaries makes it reasonably capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 31, 2026 cash and short-term-investment balance by legal entity, identify subsidiary operating and committed cash requirements, apply the relevant minority ownership claims, and rerun the bridge using only cash attributable and distributable to REX common shareholders.

audit_findings.title: Cash may be double-counted against the unfinished expansion and sequestration program
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.8 million to $38.8 million remaining against the filed $220 million to $230 million budget after $191.2 million spent; $0.86 to $1.16 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unspent project cost should reduce bridge cash if the scenarios include earnings or growth purchased by that spending.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect total capital expenditures related to the construction at the One Earth facilities to approximate $220 million to $230 million, inclusive of the carbon sequestration project and plant capacity expansion and ongoing efforts to reduce CI scoring, which we currently plan to pay from our available cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The double-counting remains possible because the valuation does not explicitly reconcile project economics with reserved cash. However, reserving the entire computed remaining budget would reduce scenario equity values by only 2.2% to 3.7%, or $0.86 to $1.16 per share. All reported scenario values are already below the $41.46 market price, so this correction would reinforce rather than change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document whether each scenario includes expansion or sequestration benefits and reserve $28.8 million to $38.8 million where it does; rerun the bridge, and reopen materiality if updated project costs exceed the filed budget materially.

audit_findings.title: Attributable earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income may have been combined with 100% consolidated depreciation, maintenance capital expenditure, working-capital and lease adjustments, producing OE for inconsistent ownership claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Net Income Attributable to Noncontrolling Interests – Income attributable to noncontrolling interests was approximately $12.1 million and $13.3 million during fiscal years 2025 and 2024, respectively, and represents the other owners’ share of the income of NuGen and One Earth.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that attributable income excludes noncontrolling interests—$12.1 million in fiscal 2025 and $8.928 million in the first six months of fiscal 2026—while consolidated cash-flow adjustments include the subsidiaries in full. The supplied record does not show the OE calculation by entity, and the net effect could raise or lower OE depending on the relationship among depreciation, maintenance capital and working-capital adjustments. Materiality therefore cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Produce an entity-level OE reconciliation for REX parent, One Earth and NuGen; apply 76.1% and 99.7% ownership consistently to every adjustment, then rerun all scenarios and compare with the current $56.1 million anchor.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method income may exceed cash economically available from Big River
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.756 million six-month 2026 excess of $10.761 million equity income over $2.005 million dividends, equal to 15.6% of the $56.1 million anchor; $14.9 million proportionate restricted net assets at January 31, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Big River accounting income enters OE even when debt restrictions and investee maintenance capital prevent equivalent distributions to REX.
audit_findings.evidence: Big River has debt agreements that limit and restrict amounts the entity can pay in the form of dividends or advances to owners.
audit_findings.explanation: Distribution restrictions are demonstrated, and the latest six-month gap between equity income and cash dividends is large relative to the anchor. Retained earnings are not necessarily valueless, but the record does not establish that they are distributable or separately create equivalent value. Capitalizing the full accounting income is therefore reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Big River maintenance capital expenditures, covenant calculations, distribution capacity and a multiyear equity-income-to-distribution reconciliation; rerun OE using normalized distributable earnings or separately value retained earnings supported by demonstrated incremental returns.
